nodes.title: Gate 2's proof becomes a battery of habit children run through served sessions (blind guess, one slip, the same slip every level, a constant answer, what I did last time, first/last/middle option, reading across), each named in under 1 session in 10; two sightings must be two different acts; an order act is confirmed on the same level; before naming the facts row carries right or wrong, first try and checks only; the unit is the child's day. Reverse if a judge finds a missing habit child in two modes after a passed battery: repeat-based naming is dropped for games

Gate 2 first reading: three Opus judges, one per mode, all FAIL; every table figure reproduced. stambh/tally: 'types 16 every level' named in 0.95 of fade-2 served sessions, 'what I typed last time' 0.38, keep five from one level. kon/place: the same keypad slip every level 0.10 (0.19 at fade 2), '75' every level 0.17; 44% of measure sessions repeat a key in their first four levels. kon/name: a swap of two taps every level 1.0, a missed tap with the letter added last 0.59

A rule that names a mix-up on a repeat is exactly what a habit triggers (the same number, slip or order on every level), and 'the two levels differ' stops only habits that depend on the level. The three gate 2 proofs modelled a blind guess and a single slip on independent levels and were never run on served sessions; the judges found each hole by running the real server path
